newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ retail price data seen helping mkt rates ease.
newsitem.headline: NZ retail price data seen helping mkt rates ease.

text.p: A 2.4 percent fall in New Zealand's February retail sales on Wednesday should further fuel the easier interest rate sentiment generated by surprisingly soft quarterly inflation data on Tuesday, analysts said.
"A number like that couldn't have come at a better time as far as the market's concerned," said ANZ economist David Drage.
"It really helped to reinforce the message given by a weaker inflation number yesterday," he told Reuters.
Core inflation came in at 0.22 percent for the March quarter and 1.97 percent for the year, against RBNZ (central bank) expectations of 0.5 percent and 2.2 percent.
Financial markets reacted immediately, easing monetary conditions by pushing debt market interest rates and the New Zealand dollar lower.

A bout of profit-taking and lingering inflation concerns stalled the easing momentum early on Wednesday, but analysts said the retail trade statistics during the morning reinforced the perception that conditions remain tighter than necessary.
"Following on from yesterday's CPI (Consumer Price Index), today's (retail) data will keep the market in easing mode," Bankers Trust said in a investment commentary.
Economists polled by Reuters had on average forecast a seasonally adjusted 0.45 percent fall in February retail sales.
Last year's leap year may have weakened this February's figure slightly, but the 2.4 percent fall reported was still well below market expecations.
"You also have to allow for the fact that it's a reasonably volatile series and most people don't pay as much attention to it as what we perhaps used to," said a money market dealer.
"But it definitely reinforces the easing picture," he added.
He said profit-taking after Tuesday's rally, and the currency's lower Trade-Weighted Index (TWI), would cap short-term rates from further rallies at present.
"The other thing you've got is that the United States is in tightening mode at the moment and, given that, you would expect us to run a little bit tighter than we would otherwise.
"But I think you will see conditions ease a little more. We're still running about 20 points too tight so at some stage we may see that crunch in a little bit more."
The 90-day bank bill was trading at 7.4 percent at 1.30 p.m. (0130 GMT) on Wednesday, about 15 basis points lower than its level prior to the release of the inflation data on Tuesday.
The TWI was at 68.39 compared to a firmer 68.74 yesterday.
